Threshold Conversations | The Roadless Rule with Ben Goldfarb

Threshold
Nov 18 2025 • 24 mins
Last June, the U.S. the Secretary of Agriculture announced that the Trump administration intends to repeal something called the “Roadless Rule”—a policy implemented in 2001, which protected some of the Forest Service’s wildest lands from logging, mining, and road-building.
Author Ben Goldfarb examined the impacts of road and roadless areas in his 2023 book, Crossings: How Road Ecology is Shaping the Future of Our Planet . We talk with Ben about why our Forest Service lands already have so many roads, and what building more would actually mean for wildlife and for people.
Threshold is nonprofit, listener-supported, and independently produced. You can support Threshold by donating today . To stay connected, sign up for our newsletter .
Credits: Threshold Conversations is produced by Sam Moore. Our music is by Todd Sickafoose. Amy Martin is our host and executive producer.

Why Did the Grizzly Bear Cross the Road?

Working Wild U
Aug 20 2026 • 25 mins
Working lands help give expanding grizzly populations room to roam - but highways can turn those connected landscapes into isolated islands.
In this episode, we follow the movement of grizzlies across the Northern Rockies and explore how roads can become barriers to bears and other wildlife. From a bear that approached I-90 47 times before finally crossing, to a stretch of Highway 93 in Montana where vehicle collisions are a major source of grizzly mortality, we dig into the science of what grizzlies need to cross a road.
Environmental journalist and author Ben Goldfarb takes us into the emerging field of road ecology, while wildlife managers with the Confederated Salish and Kootenai Tribes and the US Fish & Wildlife Service show us how wildlife crossings can reconnect habitat and make highways safer for people and animals.
But a crossing is only as useful as the land it connects. What will it take to keep those landscapes intact, too?

Alvin (Al) Goldfarb is president emeritus and professor emeritus of theatre at Western Illinois University.
